Well-motivated problem formulation articulating the tension between personalization and generalization in prompt tuning methods
Practical design with communication and parameter efficiency—only shared projection communicated, lightweight bottleneck structure
Strong baselines (5 state-of-the-art federated prompt learning methods) and multiple evaluation metrics including harmonic mean
Clear presentation, good organization, effective figures, proper technical exposition

strengths: Clear motivation and well-articulated problem addressing the personalization-generalization trade-off in federated VLM learning
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 11 datasets with multiple scenarios (base-to-novel, label/feature shifts, varying shots)
Significant communication efficiency: only 3,072 parameters communicated per round vs 8,192+ for competitors, with detailed cost analysis
Thorough ablation studies systematically justifying design choices (α, adapter dimension, starting layer, sharing strategies)
Strong empirical results in harmonic mean accuracy, consistently outperforming recent baselines (pFedMoAP, FedOTP, FedPGP) across most benchmarks
Faster convergence demonstrated in learning curves with stable training dynamics
Technically sound method with clear algorithm specification and reasonable reproducibility information
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: multi-modal adapter architecture from Yang et al. (2024); contribution is primarily application to federated learning rather than fundamental innovation
No theoretical analysis or convergence guarantees—purely empirical work; lacks principled justification for why asymmetric updates work
